currentInjectionMouldingStandards.title: Perform process operations for injection moulding
Control and optimise the injection moulding production process
Set up advanced moulds for injection moulding
Carry out routine service of injection moulding equipment
Service and maintain a complex mould for injection moulding
Set and remove complex injection moulds

learningOutcomes.text: Explain the injection-moulding cycle, production purpose, hazards and safe operating boundaries.
Explain major machine functions and distinguish setpoints, actual process signals and machine limitations.
Explain how polymer structure, rheology, moisture, additives and thermal history affect process behaviour using grade-specific evidence where required.
Explain mould, feed, cooling, venting, ejection and hot-runner functions and identify tooling evidence needed before intervention.
Explain routine service and maintenance evidence, including pre-condition, intervention, post-condition and recovery verification.
Plan and interpret controlled process studies and process-window evidence without converting generic examples into production recipes.
Diagnose moulding defects using competing mechanisms, controlled evidence and safe escalation decisions.
Interpret basic measurement, capability, monitoring and quality-record evidence and document a defensible decision trail.
Explain advanced mould setup, verification and multi-cavity considerations while preserving machine-, mould- and site-specific authority boundaries.
Demonstrate, under authorised provider/workplace control, the ability to gather practical evidence and escalate conditions outside personal authority.

mappingRule: Chapter-to-standard references indicate potentially relevant supporting knowledge or practice context only. They do not assert that a chapter covers all outcomes, evidence requirements, range statements, special notes or CMR obligations of a standard.

workplaceEvidence: evidence of escalation outside learner authority
boundaries: simulation is not workplace practical competence
a quiz pass is not consent to assess
MouldMaster completion is not an NZQA result
provider assessment does not become national-standard assessment without consent and moderation where DASS standards are used

moderationModel.internalModeration: Provider-owned and required for controlled assessment practice.
moderationModel.nationalExternalModeration: National external moderation is required through the relevant standard-setting body system when assessing DASS standards.
moderationModel.cmr: CMR 13 applies to the current Injection Moulding standards listed here.
moderationModel.repositoryRole: MouldMaster may supply draft instruments, source trails and audit fields but cannot self-grant moderation acceptance.

microCredentialReadiness.applicationOwnership: Eligible provider or other body permitted by current NZQA rules; provider accreditation remains provider-owned.
microCredentialReadiness.rule: Do not infer title, level or credits from app structure or screen time.

gates.requirement: Eligible NZQA-recognised provider and accountable application owner confirmed.
Documented employer, learner, provider and industry need/support evidence.
Final title, outcomes, NZQCF level, credit/workload, entry, RPL/credit, assessment and completion rules approved by provider.
Approved summative instruments, authorised assessors, internal moderation and evidence-retention controls.
Consent to assess and CMR 13 capability where current DASS standards are assessed.
Participation in the relevant national external moderation system where standards are assessed.
Real workplace evidence under authorised conditions; simulations and app records cannot substitute for required practical evidence.
Provider-controlled formal review cycle, stakeholder review, change governance and NZQA change-consent handling.
